answer: A proof-of-burn registry curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to verifiably destroy native tokens to mint credentials. Registrations route through a juniper filter to an admission jetty that enforces strict rate limits. An attacker spawning multiple identities incurs an unrecoverable capital cost per key, creating an economic canyon that renders mass replication expensive. However, this barrier disadvantages low-capital agents and enables wealthy adversaries to acquire undue influence.
